title: Affine tops and representable matroids
claim: (1) In a law that composes like cycles, let B be a knot range. The parallelogram relation of any knot through B (four copies arranged as a two-by-two square) has as top image the graph of the operation induced on B's top by any polymorphism Mal'tsev modulo that top; so that operation is unique and its graph is pp-definable. Every polymorphism commutes with it; it is x - y + z for an abelian group structure on the top, which is elementary abelian of some prime exponent; every polymorphism acts on the top by affine maps; and the top image of every system, restricted to variables with knot ranges, is a coset of a subgroup. (2) Every three-variable circuit is, modulo the tops and after relabelling, the addition table of an elementary abelian p-group. (3) Every system's matroid is a direct sum of rank-one parallel classes and matroids representable over finite fields, the field of a component being the endomorphism field of its tops as modules over the ring of linear parts of the polymorphisms; this proves the weak form of Conjecture 5 of MATROID-CONVERSE-20261021-001B-P001. Conversely every direct sum of matroids representable over finite fields is carried by a system of some law that composes like cycles.
failure_conditions: In a law that composes like cycles, a knot's parallelogram relation is not the graph of one Mal'tsev operation on a knot range's top, or two knots through one range give different operations.
That operation is not x - y + z for an elementary abelian p-group, a polymorphism does not commute with it, or a top image restricted to knot-range variables is not closed under it.
A three-variable circuit's top image is not an addition table after relabelling.
A system of a law that composes like cycles carries a matroid with a component of rank two or more that is representable over no finite field, or a variable without a knot range in such a component.
foundation_claim_scope: Which laws compose like cycles: affine structure on the tops of knot ranges and the matroids carried. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies on 1,200 random systems over fifteen laws (census laws with certified tops, 3-nets of Z4, Z2xZ2 and Z2xZ4, and a GF(4) law with a certified top) that every knot's parallelogram relation is the graph of one Mal'tsev operation per range, self-commuting, equal to x - y + z of an elementary abelian group, that top images are closed under it, that searched polymorphisms induce it and commute with it, that three-variable circuits are addition tables, and that matroids are represented over the predicted fields (U(2,4) over GF(4)); four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with randomized checks; AFFINE-TOPS-20261021-001A-P001, the overlap proof's Theorem 2, the Galois connection between polymorphisms and pp-definable relations, Wedderburn's theorem and the density theorem are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta: Theorem 1 (affine knot tops), Corollary 2 and Theorem 3 (matroids in R over finite fields, proving the weak form of Conjecture 5 of MATROID-CONVERSE-20261021-001B-P001) are new to the program; the steps use classical algebra (self-commuting Mal'tsev operations, the Galois connection, Wedderburn, density, Rado); analogues exist in model theory (locally modular geometries) and universal algebra (Herrmann's theorem); folklore risk moderate.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
